summary: Forwarded passwordless 'magic link' sign-in resulted in unexpected privileged session creation
summary_verbose: Customer-facing passwordless sign-in link (magic link) generated by internal admin console was forwarded externally and used to create a long-lived privileged session for an internal admin account. Suspect phishing + session lifetime escalation bug.
description: Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 an internal admin used the admin console to generate a passwordless (magic) login link for convenience. That link was forwarded externally from the admin's personal mailbox. The link was subsequently used to establish an authenticated session from an IP associated with a privacy/VPN provider and an observed Tor exit node. The session acquired elevated privileges because the account had a recent temporary role grant (automation) that overlapped with the sign-in window. Impact: potential unauthorized access to internal admin functions (user role assignments, service account listing). No confirmed data exfiltration yet; audit logs show listing and a single attempt to view a service-account key creation page which was not completed. This ticket coordinates triage, containment, and postmortem actions.
timeline:
2026-03-10 09:22 UTC: Admin generated magic link via admin-console
2026-03-10 09:26 UTC: Link forwarded from personal gmail to external address (user-reported)
2026-03-10 09:31 UTC: Auth logs show token redemption from 185.88.163.12 (VPN provider) and 185.220.101.1 (Tor exit candidate)
2026-03-10 09:33 UTC: Session created with session_id sess_3f9a and assigned temporary role 'prod-admin-temp'
2026-03-10 09:40 UTC: Alerts triggered by anomalous admin console navigation

steps_to_reproduce: Generate magic link from admin console for account alice.patel@redwood.com
Forward link to an external mailbox
Redeem link from an IP associated with a VPN/Tor node
Observe session creation and role assignment in auth logs
logs_observations: auth-service logs: token_redeem sess_3f9a from 185.88.163.12 user=alice.patel@redwood.com scope=ui:admin
iam-service logs: applied role prod-admin-temp to alice.patel@redwood.com during session sess_3f9a
console-audit: GET /service-accounts?list=true by alice.patel@redwood.com session=sess_3f9a status=200 (read only)
no service-account key create POST observed in audit trail (attempt aborted)
session expiry observed: 72h (unexpectedly long for magic-link sessions)
initial_triage: Team notes: Likely chain = user forwarded link (human error) + reuse from anonymizing IP + automation timing caused temporary high privileges to be in effect. Two actionable risk areas: magic-link forwarding risk & role-grant automation overlap. Need to contain session, rotate any exposed ephemeral tokens, review magic-link lifetime defaults, and check if this pattern could be automated by an attacker.
actions_taken: Invalidated session sess_3f9a and all active magic-link tokens for alice.patel@redwood.com at 2026-03-10 10:15 UTC
Forced logout for alice.patel@redwood.com across all devices
Revoked temporary role prod-admin-temp and blocked the role-grant automation pending review
Contacted the admin to confirm they forwarded the link and collected the external mailbox address for follow-up
Raised a priority incident in #security-ops and paged oncall SRE
evidence_collected: auth-service raw token redemption entry id=auth-76821
pcap request headers from CloudEdge WAF for 185.88.163.12 (saved)
admin's sent-mail header showing forward event to suspicious external email
current_risk_assessment: Medium-High: attacker had admin UI read/list capabilities for ~12 minutes; no destructive actions observed. Risk of lateral movement depends on whether any API keys or full-service-account pages were accessed and on whether forwarded inbox was compromised.
next_steps: Confirm whether forwarded external mailbox owner is benign (contact outbound security) and request that they delete the link email
Short-term mitigation: reduce magic-link session TTL to 15 minutes and require IP confirmation for admin roles
Long-term: add UI warning + block forwarding (Content-Security/Email headers) and instrument magic link redemption with stricter device fingerprint checks
Audit automation: change role-grant jobs to avoid granting high privileges in windows following magic-link issuance
Schedule postmortem with security and platform teams and update runbook
